messages:
Priya: Quick sync — oncall saw ~600 SLO alerts in the last 24h after a few customers flipped the console "notify on breach" default. We need to reduce noise and give better visibility before they hit PD.
Tom: whoa. any idea which routes/models triggered most? :eyes:
Priya: mostly high-traffic routes with transient latency spikes. One tenant had a bad rollout which amplified volume.
Lei: this is the console UX problem + default policy. Idea: show an "estimated alert volume" preview when users edit thresholds or turn on notifications. It should use past 30d telemetry and the route's QPS/latency distribution.
Riya: aggro alerts are burning pages. We should also wire dedupe/fanout controls into the SLO config so users can choose "one incident per window" or "per-route fanout". Defaults should be conservative.
Jorge: UX idea — instead of raw numbers, show a small histogram + expected notifs/day and a toggle for "canary rollout" for alerting (10% traffic -> preview). That lets teams test without blasting PD.
Tom: agree. For the PD/Slack integration, we need to decide whether console exposes a per-tenant fanout target (e.g., 3 recipients) or we keep routing in our alert router.
Lei: API debate: do we expose alerting config in the public API? Pros: infra-as-code, customers can automate. Cons: surface for abuse and accidental wide rollouts. Proposal: public read + write via API only if tenant has "infra-managed" flag. Otherwise UI-only with audit logs.
Riya: also add a preview mode that simulates notifications without actually sending. That helps SREs test throttle behavior. Maybe a label "dry_run": true on the config.
Priya: sample preview response we could show in console:
```
{
  "route": "text.generate",
  "qps": 120,
  "threshold_ms": 800,
  "estimated_alerts_24h": 42,
  "estimated_pages_24h": 6
}
```
Lei: implementation notes: backend needs a light-weight estimator service that takes route metrics + config and returns counts. Cache estimates for 5m. Add a small charge? keep free.
Tom: operationally we also want auto-suppression for known rollouts. If a rollout is flagged in the rollout API, suppress noisy SLO alerts for X minutes and instead surface a rollout-warning event.
Riya: +1. And we should default notify_channel to "console" (in-product) and require explicit opt-in for PD/Slack until teams confirm expected volume.
Jorge: tiny UI polish — show a red/orange/green bar that maps to estimated pages/day so non-SRE users grok noise.
Priya: decision proposed: 1) add "estimated alert volume" preview to threshold edit flow; 2) default to conservative fanout and in-product notifications; 3) add canary rollout toggle for alert rules; 4) expose API write only for infra-managed tenants. I'll draft a short RFC and assign owners.
Tom: sounds good. I'll follow up with a short oncall runbook for suppressed alerts and how to opt-in.
pagerduty-bot: Incident routed to PD team "infra-oncall" (simulated) :information_source:
Priya: assigning Lei to backend estimator + Jorge for the UI mock. Riya/Tom to define default fanout and suppression windows. I'll post the RFC by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
